descriptive_title: Grade 2 Mathematics: Demonstrations — Equivalent Money Combinations (F1.1)
subject: Mathematics

curriculum_expectations.F1.1: identify different ways of representing the same amount of money up to Canadian 200¢ using various combinations of coins, and up to $200 using various combinations of $1 and $2 coins and $5, $10, $20, $50, and $100 bills

unit_overview: A 5-day Grade 2 unit on equivalent money combinations (F1.1) framed around 'Tap to Pay' — Tappy the Toonie Frog and Loonie Lou the Mouse. Day 1 reviews coins and shows MULTIPLE WAYS to make 50¢. Day 2 makes 100¢ ($1) with different coin combinations. Day 3 makes $2-$50 amounts using bills and coins. Day 4 introduces the $100 bill and amounts up to $200. Day 5 closes with a Big Tap-to-Pay Capstone where children find equivalent ways to pay. Each lesson includes an expanded_walkthrough.
unit_learning_goal: Children will represent the same amount of money in different ways using coin and bill combinations up to $200.

lesson_arc.big_idea: Same AMOUNT, different COINS. 50¢ = 2 quarters = 5 dimes = 50 pennies (historical).
lesson_arc.student_learning_goal: I can make 50¢ in 3 different ways.
lesson_arc.one_line_summary: Tappy shows 3 ways; children find their own combinations.

lesson_arc.student_learning_goal: I can make $1 in 3 different ways.
lesson_arc.one_line_summary: Loonie Lou shows; children find $1 combos.

lesson_arc.big_idea: BIG amounts use BILLS. $25 = 2 tens + 1 fiver = 1 twenty + 1 fiver = many ways.
lesson_arc.student_learning_goal: I can mix bills and coins to make amounts up to $50.
lesson_arc.one_line_summary: Tappy makes $25 three ways; children try $35.

lesson_arc.big_idea: The $100 bill is BROWN. We make amounts up to $200 with bills and coins.
lesson_arc.student_learning_goal: I can make amounts up to $200.
lesson_arc.one_line_summary: Loonie Lou shows the $100; children make $150.

lesson_arc.big_idea: Same AMOUNT, MANY WAYS. We pick the way that uses the FEWEST or RIGHT bills.
lesson_arc.student_learning_goal: I can find different ways to pay an amount.
lesson_arc.one_line_summary: Children find 3 ways to pay each of 4 amounts.

recurring_characters.name: Tappy the Toonie Frog
recurring_characters.role: Lead character. Coin combo expert. Anchors all 5 lessons.
recurring_characters.visual_description: A cheerful frog with a toonie around its neck and a tap-to-pay card.

recurring_characters.name: Loonie Lou the Mouse
recurring_characters.role: Tappy's partner. Bill expert. Cameo Lessons 3-5.
recurring_characters.visual_description: A small mouse with a loonie pendant and a stack of bills.

threaded_vocabulary.child_friendly_definition: Same VALUE, different COINS or BILLS.
A MIX of coins and bills.
The smallest NUMBER of coins or bills.
Exactly EQUAL — no more, no less.
Modern way: tap a card, pay exactly.

pedagogical_notes: Grade 2 expands G1 from identification to EQUIVALENCE.
Children must SEE that 2 quarters = 5 dimes (same amount, different coins).
Use real coin cards — make it tactile.
Up to $200 means children handle $100 bill — show its features.
Tap-to-pay frame brings money up to date — modern Canadian context.
canadian_context_notes: $100 bill is BROWN with Robert Borden.
Tap-to-pay debit and credit cards used widely in Canada.
Tim Hortons combos used for amount examples.
